text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures flitted to session highs in late trade after regional inflation data suggested price pressure remains subdued. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.69, up 0/23 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended virtually flat and will remain wedged in a narrow trading range until Wednedsay's retail sales data and five-year auction are out of the way, with sales forecast up 0.3 pct in March, auction expected to be covered about two times. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-14/32, unchanged from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures remained rangebound during a nervous session as traders awaited the first opinion polls of voters' intentions for the upcoming May 25 parliamentary election. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.42, up 0.14 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and Btp futures recovered ground recouping most of the session's losses by the close after a bumpy day with the market awaiting the last five Italian cities' April CPI data which might lead to a Bank of Italy rate cut. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.38, down 0.01 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury securities prices remained range bound at midday as players awaited the results of Treasury's auction of two-year notes. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-27/32, up 06/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.08 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed slightly firmer after the new 10-year JGB auction went as expected. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 127.05, up 0.05 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Activity was quite brisk, but mainstream dollar deals remained absent due to an uncertain market. "There is still a lot of nervousness among investors," a syndicate manager at a European bank said. "The U.S. Treasury market is considered a bit shaky, and European elections, like in France, are adding some uncertainty there.
